abstract: classical natural philosophy sought the natural law governing the motion of free bodies long before daring to construct the appropriate mathematical formalism. following this longstanding methodological perspective, in the present work general relativity is reconstructed from operational and dynamical principles, rather than taking spacetime geometry as its starting point. the \textit{conatus} of a massive free particle is identified with its natural tendency to follow a worldline of stationary proper time, which, under the appropriate local conditions, corresponds to a maximum of its proper time, whereas gravitation is interpreted as the \textit{potentia} of matter to modify the local rate of proper time. by requiring the exact validity of galilean free fall, the weak-field static invariant is determined. the gravitational field of moving sources is subsequently obtained by lorentz-transforming the elementary static solution and causally superposing the retarded contributions of infinitesimal source elements. the resulting linearized field equations coincide with those of general relativity in the harmonic gauge. finally, imposing general energy-momentum conservation together with the requirement of second-order field equations yields--- within the class of theories satisfying the stated assumptions and by virtue of lovelock's theorem---the unique covariant completion represented by einstein's field equations. within this construction, geometry is not postulated from the outset; instead, it emerges as the final mathematical synthesis of operational dynamics based on proper time, inertia, and free fall.

title: first-order structure of the linearised einstein equations: constant-curvature backgrounds
abstract: teukolsky's decoupled equations and wald's adjoint method of metric reconstruction are built from second-order operators: the linearised einstein operator g, the curvature-extraction operator t, the decoupled operator o and the reconstruction operator s^*, related by sg=ot. we show that on four-dimensional constant-curvature backgrounds with non-zero lambda all of these operators factor into first-order maps through a single intermediate variable: the perturbation of the self-dual half of the spin connection. we also show that for non-zero lambda the metric perturbation is itself obtained from the connection perturbation by a first-order map. the connection therefore gives a complete description of linearised gravity, and the fourth-order identity sg=ot follows by composition from a single second-order identity. using conformal flatness, we choose the hertz-potential map so that, after a conformal rescaling, the potential obeys the flat wave equation component by component. this leads to a new reconstruction scheme, in which the potential is sourced by the curvature psi, which in turn obeys a decoupled sourced equation. a prescribed curvature is then reached by a second-order rather than a fourth-order equation, and the corrector is local and algebraic in the stress-energy tensor. the price is that the full curvature, rather than a single component, must be determined, and that the reality of the reconstructed metric becomes a condition, which we argue holds for retarded solutions. we illustrate the scheme for a static point mass in de sitter space, where it gives a real metric perturbation that agrees with linearised schwarzschild-de sitter up to a diffeomorphism. we view these results as a proof of concept for a first-order teukolsky-wald framework on kerr.

title: tracking the evolution of supermassive black hole binaries with pulsar terms
abstract: pulsar timing arrays will soon be able to resolve the loudest supermassive black hole binaries contributing to the stochastic gravitational wave background at nanohertz frequencies. while the few decades of observations are typically not enough to see these binaries evolve in frequency, the so-called pulsar terms offer a glimpse into the past and can help us map out the frequency evolution of these binaries over tens of thousands of years. measuring this long-term frequency evolution can allow us to look for deviations from a vacuum binary evolution due to various environmental effects. we develop a fisher-matrix approach to calculate how precisely the frequency can be tracked over time in this manner, and demonstrate its use on a realistic near-future pulsar timing array with a 30-year baseline. we find that the environmental effects predicted by 2-dimensional hydrodynamic simulations of circumbinary disks are unlikely to be detectable in the circular binaries we considered, however, in some cases they might result in biased chirp mass recovery if ignored. we also demonstrate how this approach allows one to test the orbital evolution predicted by general relativity in a purely gravitational-wave driven inspiral, and to put upper limits on additional generic environmental effects described by a power-law hardening model.

title: relativistic plasticity
abstract: the elastic crust of a neutron star has long been established as a key player in relevant aspects of neutron star physics. however, the state-of-the-art theory of elasticity is restricted to the perturbative domain and does not account for permanent plastic deformations which should be relevant for pulsar glitches, magnetar flares, and the continuous emission of gravitational waves. plasticity, however, is a historically challenging phenomenon to model - even in the newtonian regime. this is owed mainly to its dissipative character and the multiscale methods required to consistently reproduce observed phenomena. in this work, we address this first challenge by making use of recent developments in the variational modelling of dissipative fluids to extend the theory of relativistic elasticity to include plastic phenomenology. the resulting theory possesses the same freedoms as the modern newtonian formalism, while now being compatible with general relativity. the second law of thermodynamics is then used to introduce the yield criterion of plasticity theory in the relativistic setting.

title: joint angular-power distributions of interfering nanohertz gravitational waves
abstract: finite populations of supermassive black-hole binaries produce fluctuations in both gravitational-wave power and pulsar timing correlations. we characterize the realization-dependent, orientation-averaged earth-term angular correlation through its frequency-resolved legendre coefficients. a hybrid model of bright sources and a gaussian faint background extends the conditional gamma distribution in the many-weak-source limit to non-central $χ^2$ statistics, yielding correlated multipoles after population marginalization. our analytical variance decomposition and smbhb population simulations reveal a population-dependent transition from interference dominated variance at low frequencies to population-power-dominated variance at high frequencies. in the many-weak-source regime, a multivariate lognormal approximation captures the main features of the joint distribution using only the first two log-cumulants. these results provide statistical benchmarks for fluctuations in both the overall amplitude and angular structure of the realized correlation.
